biggestGap: Three of the six fruits — watermelon, apple, orange — are still outline-identical smooth balls: every authored appendage (0.115r stem, 0.54-long apple stem, 0.165 navel, five 6.2% lobes) is a surface-shading event only and none of them reaches the silhouette, so the fruit that anchors the hero can be swapped for the apple without the outline changing.
evidence: Predecessor's probe reproduced exactly (max-channel luminance, threshold 8, 640x360, bbox-centre radial trace at 720 rays — verified by re-hitting r2's numbers 53.72/2.43/0.0452 against their quoted 53.90/2.53/0.047). shots/r3/01-whole-watermelon.png: bbox 144x131, aspect 1.099 (r2 108x108/1.000, r2b 140x142/0.986); height fraction 36.4% of 360 px (r2 30.0%, r2b 39.4%, plate-01 61.1%) — so scale went UP vs r2 but DOWN vs r2b and is still 25 points short of the plate. Radial trace std/mean 0.1052 vs r2's 0.0452 — a genuine 2.3x, and the FFT confirms it is a real prolate axis (k=2 amplitude 7.22 px on mean r 68.99 = 10.5%, vs r2b's 5.02/71.81 = 7.0%), which matches the authored rx/ry/rz 1.0/1.17/0.862 in src/fruit/geometry.js:233. But the +21.2% radial maximum sits at 319 deg, on the key side — that is the same rim-glow bloom lobe the r2 critic called out, not the stem. Masking the warm bloom out (green-dominant mask, t=12) leaves a clean body outline of 117x123 with ZERO protrusion anywhere: the 0.115r/0.31-long stem is visible as a dark nub against the peel but contributes nothing to the boundary, and it is absent entirely from shots/r3/00-hero.png. High-frequency boundary energy (k>20) is 0.17 px rms — no polygon facets, that auto-fail is clear. Hero: the two melon halves span 203x260 px = 36.1% of 720, i.e. the hero framing was NOT enlarged past the standard shot and both halves show the lat-long pole rosette face-on, so the stem axis is pointing down the camera. Crown verdict: YES, it stopped reading as a hand of bananas — shots/r3/12-idle-blade.png shows flat, pointed, leaf-profile blades off ONE pole (r2b's same shot is unambiguously fat blunt tubes / sea urchin); it now reads as a palm frond or feather duster, gold like the body rather than plate-01's green, curved, as long as the body and fanning ~200 deg instead of a whorl. Identifiable by outline alone: strawberry (cone + spiked calyx, confirmed in 09 crop) and pineapple-ish (leafy top). Apple in 10/11 measures 114x106 and is a bare green ball with no stem, no calyx basin, no five-lobe waist visible; orange is a pitted 104x110 ball with a ~4 px nub. Root cause is src/play/director.js:79, which still sets a uniformly random Euler — geometry.js's own header even says the orientation bias is 'NOT IN THIS FILE'.
fix: src/play/director.js line 79: replace the uniform `setFromEuler(rr(0,6.28) x3)` with an orientation that first picks a random azimuth about the view axis, then constrains the fruit's +Y (the stem/well/crown axis) to lie within ~30-40 deg of the camera's screen plane — i.e. sample the polar tilt from acos(u*0.6) rather than uniformly on the sphere. Every appendage in geometry.js is authored on +Y, so it can only break the limb when +Y is near-perpendicular to the view; right now half of all spawns look straight down the pole and the stem, the well and the navel all collapse into a shading detail on a circle. Do this before spending any more on appendage size — the 0.115r stem is already 6x the 4 px visibility floor and still measures zero.
